- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for rebound potential.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., 73+), overshooting by 2–5% in 3–5 day horizon; apply dampening factor of 0.95–0.98 to peak forecasts.  
- If 3+ consecutive days of negative sentiment, model underestimates; apply upward bias of 1–2% to offset mean reversion bias.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags 1–2 days behind true trend; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for lagged momentum.  
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; force a 1–2% downward correction at the shift point.  
- If true outcome is below 60% of 30d mean, model overestimates; apply downward correction proportional to sentiment volatility (e.g., 0.5–1.5% per 0.10 sentiment drop).
